newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Businessmen accuse Manila banks of opportunism.
newsitem.headline: Businessmen accuse Manila banks of opportunism.

text.p: Philippine businessmen on Wednesday accused local banks of opportunism following last Friday's effective devaluation of the peso.

"The Federation of Philippine Industries ... blamed many of the commercial banks as opportunistic and insensitive to their clients by taking advantage of the rapid depreciation of the peso," the Federation said in a statement.
"Why are banks buying dollars at 27 to 28 pesos and selling it to their clients who need dollars to pay for their imports at 31 to 33 pesos?"
It noted the spread of four to five pesos compared to the usual four centavos per dollar.
The peso has fallen about 11.5 percent since Friday's move by the central bank when it caved in to speculative attacks and allowed it to move in a wider band.
The Federation also questioned why banks were using the central bank's 25 percent one-month reverse repo rate to establish their own lending rates.
Commercial bank prime rates have more than doubled in the past month and are currently as high as 35 percent.
"We want to know the rationale for this move. After all, less than 20 percent of the loans extended by the commercial bank come from borrowings from the central bank," it said.
